memory_candidates.content: A bash lib assigning a heredoc-sourced variable via `read -r -d '' VAR <<'EOF' ... EOF` always returns exit status 1 at EOF (no NUL delimiter is ever found in a heredoc), even though the assignment itself fully succeeds. Sourcing such a lib with a bare top-level `source file` inside a `set -e` script aborts the sourcing script right at that line -- before any function later in the file is even defined. The established, working pattern in this codebase (task-lock.sh's ensure_file_scope_overlap_lib()) is to source via `if ! . file 2>/dev/null; then <error>; fi`, which is exempt from set -e's abort-on-failure because it is the direct condition of an if-statement. Any NEW caller of scripts/lib/file-scope-overlap.sh (or any other lib using this read -d '' idiom) under set -e must use the same if-guarded form, never a bare source.

Several scratch-fixture test suites under scripts/ (test-conflict-predicate.sh, test-four-tier-conflict.sh, test-session-registry.sh, test-state-write-concurrency.sh, test-state-write-large-payload.sh, test-state-write-regen-timing.sh, test-task-lock-reap.sh, test-postflight-deploy-gate.sh) copy task-lock.sh into an isolated .claude/scripts/ tree but never copy lib/task-lookup-lib.sh, which task-lock.sh sources unconditionally near its top. Every one of these fixtures therefore fails at task-lock.sh invocation time with 'lib/task-lookup-lib.sh: No such file or directory', independent of whatever the suite is actually trying to test. This is a real, pre-existing, unrelated repo defect (confirmed via git log that task-lock.sh's task-lookup-lib.sh dependency predates any of several recent, unrelated tasks) worth fixing as its own small task: add lib/task-lookup-lib.sh to each fixture's copy list.
